sources.citation: McLafferty & Turecek, Interpretation of Mass Spectra, 4th ed., University Science Books, 1993
MØD Rule.fromDFS encodings in src/data_generation/rules/ (German-edition provenance)

evidence.curator_note: Radical-site hydrogen rearrangement in n-ionized 1-chloropentane: the Cl-centred odd electron abstracts a hydrogen three carbons away (a five-membered, i.e. not six-membered, transition state - the book stresses this), giving H-Cl+ and a secondary C-radical (the middle structure). Book draws 3 arcs; moves <1,2,3> are all drawn (small hook returning one C-H electron to the carbon, large S-sweep carrying the other C-H electron to the forming H-Cl bond, and the check-mark fishhook feeding the Cl radical electron into that H-Cl bond) - a fully depicted three-fishhook H-atom transfer, no implicit hook. The migrating hydrogen (map 7) is written as [1H] - ordinary protium with its isotope pinned, NOT deuterium - solely so RDKit's default parser retains it as a mapped atom (plain mapped [H] is stripped by removeHs), letting the C-H and H-Cl bond changes be bookkept.

Charge-site (inductive) cleavage: the Cl+ charge site draws the C-Cl bonding pair onto chlorine, expelling neutral HCl and leaving the charge on the carbon skeleton - McLafferty's 'charge migration' path. Book draws 1 arc; move <1> is drawn, a single full (two-barbed) curved arrow from the C-Cl bond onto Cl (electron_count 2). The book draws the ionic product as ethylcyclopropane radical cation (m/z 70); a cyclopropane radical cation has no valence-valid two-electron Lewis structure (the three-membered ring cannot stay intact while carrying a localized charge + radical), so it is encoded here as the equivalent ring-opened 1,3-distonic radical cation - primary carbocation at the former C-Cl carbon (map 2) plus the secondary C-radical (map 4) - which the single inductive arrow produces exactly (same formula C5H10, m/z 70). Ring closure of that 1,3 radical/cation pair to the drawn cyclopropane is a subsequent radical-cation combination not separately drawn.

Cross-linked MØD rules IMS_4_40_rH and IMS_4_40_ind (rule_index by_equation 4.40). VERIFIED against their DFS: IMS_4_40_rH cleaves a C-H bond and forms the Cl-H bond, converting Cl+. to even-electron Cl+ and creating the C radical - identical bond changes to step_rH; it matches this substrate. IMS_4_40_ind cleaves the C-Cl bond to neutral HCl (both electrons to Cl - the same inductive move as step_ind) AND simultaneously forms the C3-C5 ring bond (cyclopropane) marking the former C-Cl carbon as [C+.]; that ring-closed radical cation is NOT a valence-valid localized structure (the C+. carbon retains its two hydrogens and gains the ring bond, i.e. a hypervalent centre) - MØD term-mode rewriting bypasses valence so the mass (C5H10, m/z 70) is still correct, but the localized Lewis structure is not. This record therefore encodes the valence-valid ring-opened 1,3-distonic resonance form of the same m/z-70 ion; the two agree on formula, HCl loss and net connectivity change but differ in the (chemically unrepresentable) placement of the ring bond vs the localized charge/radical. See rule_mismatches.
